accepted.name: event_incidence_smoothed
accepted.description: Jeffreys-smoothed incidence proportion: the share of the at-risk cohort that experienced at least one event of this class (serious / other / death), shrunk so that a 0-of-8 arm is not scored as a hazard of exactly zero.
accepted.why_it_matters: The label is a count of affected patients; a count is exposure times hazard, and this is the hazard half. The raw ratio is unusable where it matters most - median subjects_at_risk is 29 and p25 is 10, so a third of arms report 0 events and the unsmoothed rate collapses them all onto the same 0. Values above 1 should occur only in the handful of internally inconsistent AACT rows where affected exceeds at-risk.

accepted.name: event_log_odds
accepted.description: Empirical log-odds that a given at-risk subject experienced this event class, with a half-count added to both cells so zero-event and all-event arms stay finite.
accepted.why_it_matters: Adverse-event rates span orders of magnitude (all-cause mortality in a 2M-subject registry vs a 10-person Phase 1 arm), and a proportion crammed into [0,1] gives the model almost no resolution at the low end where most rows sit. The log-odds scale is the one on which these rates are actually additive across trial and population effects. Typical values should be about -6 to +2.

accepted.name: expected_case_sd
accepted.description: Binomial standard deviation of the number of affected subjects, sqrt(n*p*(1-p)), computed from this row's own cohort - how many cases a repeat of this reporting period would plausibly differ by.
accepted.why_it_matters: The target is a count in the same units, so this states the irreducible spread of that count directly. It separates the two ways a row can report few cases: a small cohort where the count is uninformative noise, and a large cohort with a genuinely low hazard. Hard cap is sqrt(max n)/2 = 710 at the 2.02M-subject outlier.

accepted.name: reported_true_zero
accepted.description: Flags a row that affirmatively reports zero events in a non-empty at-risk cohort, as opposed to a row with no cohort at all.
accepted.why_it_matters: subjects_affected has p25 = 0 and median = 1, so this target is heavily zero-inflated, and a hard zero backed by real exposure is a genuine safety observation while an empty cohort is only an absence of reporting. Any arithmetic feature blurs the two. Note the null caveat: subjects_affected is 15.7% null and NaN == 0 is False, so nulls fall on the 0 side of this flag rather than being distinguished.

accepted.name: log_enrollment_per_arm
accepted.description: Log of the subjects enrolled per treatment arm - the size of the cohort that a single adverse-event row will actually be tabulated over.
accepted.why_it_matters: Adverse events are reported per arm, not per trial, so per-arm enrollment (not total enrollment) is the exposure that generates the count being predicted. The maximum() guard keeps the 24% of studies with a null arm count on the total-enrollment interpretation instead of dropping them to null, and the log tames a column whose max (188M) is a population registry rather than an enrolled cohort. Upper bound is log1p of that max.

rejected.name: log_ci_relative_width
rejected.description: Width of the reported confidence interval relative to the magnitude of the effect it brackets - a scale-free measure of how imprecise this trial's analyses are.
rejected.why_it_matters: Raw CI width is meaningless across analyses measured in different units (mmHg vs hazard ratio vs percent); the ratio to the point estimate is comparable across all of them and is essentially a proxy for effective sample size at the outcome level. Trials whose efficacy analyses are wide and underpowered are small trials, and small trials produce small adverse-event counts. The maximum() guards handle the inverted intervals and near-zero estimates in this table.

rejected.name: ci_asymmetry_ratio
rejected.description: How far the point estimate sits from the midpoint of its own confidence interval, as a fraction of the interval width, clipped to +/-5.
rejected.why_it_matters: Near zero means a symmetric normal-approximation interval around a difference; materially nonzero means the estimate lives on a ratio scale (hazard, odds, or risk ratio) whose interval is symmetric only after logging. That distinction is what param_type is supposed to record and often does not, and it changes what param_value even means. The explicit clip is why I can promise this range rather than guessing at the tail from ci_upper_limit's 1e9 outliers; well-formed rows should land inside +/-0.5.

rejected.name: ci_includes_null_effect
rejected.description: Flags an analysis whose confidence interval straddles zero - i.e. no significant difference was demonstrated on a difference scale.
rejected.why_it_matters: This is the conclusion a reader draws from the interval, and it takes reading two columns together rather than either alone (median lower limit is -0.23 and median upper is 1.41, so both signs are well populated). Caveat I would rather state than hide: for ratio-type parameters the null is 1, not 0, so this flag is only correct for the difference-scale subset.
